processing: Bred for green tea: the shoots are fixed, rolled and dried without oxidation, in the way usual for Yunnan greens.
harvest_season: The picking date for this cultivar is little documented; Yunnan greens are generally most prized in early spring.
appearance_liquor: Clear, as with other Yunnan greens; a pale yellow-green is the likely colour.
taste_profile: A high, long-lasting aroma and a fresh, mellow taste.

brewing.notes: Downy leaf can cloud the cup slightly, which is normal. Keep the first steep short to hold on to the aroma.

vintage_note: Rarely labelled by cultivar. Like other Yunnan greens, tea from it is sold as the current spring harvest and is best drunk within the year.
description:
Foxiang 3 is a Yunnan tea cultivar bred for aromatic green tea, and its name, Buddha fragrance, points at exactly what the breeders were after. It is a cross of Fuding Dabai with Changye Baihao, selected from a single plant in the first generation.

The finished green is covered in silver down, which reflects its bud character and shows clearly in the dry leaf. It is recommended for planting in Yunnan's large-leaf tea zone, where it adds a highly fragrant option to the usual stock.

In the cup it is described as having a high, lasting aroma and a fresh, mellow taste, with bright yellow-green spent leaves. Treat it as a green and not as a pu-erh base: water a little off the boil and short steeps.

You may see Menghai teas sold as Foxiang or Buddha Aroma, but some of these describe a different parentage, a Menghai large-leaf plant crossed with a small-leaf plant from northeast Yunnan. So a Foxiang label does not necessarily mean this numbered line. Ask the seller, and buy it fresh.
history:
Foxiang 3 was bred at the Tea Research Institute of the Yunnan Academy of Agricultural Sciences by artificial pollination of Fuding Dabai with Changye Baihao, then single-plant selection from the F1 generation. The work was reported in Acta Horticulturae Sinica in 2009, with the aim stated as a high-aroma, high-quality, high-yield, hardy green tea cultivar.

A Menghai green sold as Buddha Aroma is said by its seller to have been first developed in 1987, with different parents. How that tea relates to the numbered line is unclear.
